newsitem.title: ITALY: Jewish graves vandalised in Rome cemetery.
newsitem.headline: Jewish graves vandalised in Rome cemetery.

text.p: Vandals attacked Jewish graves in a cemetery in Rome, breaking some tombstones and ripping the names and Star of David off a number of others, police said on Sunday.
The desecration was discovered early on Sunday and around 300 people from the local Jewish community attended a ceremony to re-sanctify the site later in the day.

The vandals surrounded one tomb with barbed wire and swastikas and left the sign "Arbeit macht frei" (work brings freedom) next to a small cemetery chapel. The same words were placed over the entrance to the Auschwitz death camp in Poland where millions of Jews were killed during World War Two.
"This is definitely the work of Nazi skinheads," said the chief Rabbi in Rome, Elio Toaff. "They don't take it out on the living but only the dead," he said.
The attack was condemned by leading politicians. "Those Nazi symbols offend the democratic conscience of our country," Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said.
Police promised to hunt down the vandals.
